title: Mem^p: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
problem_statement: LLM-based agents suffer from brittle procedural memory that is manually engineered or frozen in static parameters. The paper investigates how to make procedural memory learnable, updatable, and lifelong across agent trajectories.
key_ideas: Build procedural memory by distilling trajectories into verbatim traces, abstract scripts, or both (Proceduralization = best)
Retrieve using cosine similarity over task embeddings; keyword-averaged AveFact retrieval outperforms raw query embeddings
Update with error-correction reflection (Adjustment): revise failed memories in-place, outperforming vanilla append or success-only filtering
Procedural memory from a strong model (GPT-4o) transfers to a weaker model (Qwen2.5-14B) without retraining
Formal MDP model of memory lifecycle: Add/Delete/Update operations over the memory store
method_summary: Mem^p is a task-agnostic framework with three phases: Build (construct procedural memories from trajectories via trajectory storage, script abstraction, or Proceduralization combining both), Retrieve (cosine similarity over embeddings with key construction strategies: random, query-vector, AveFact keyword-averaged), and Update (Vanilla append, Validation success-only, or Adjustment in-place error correction via reflection). No fine-tuning required; all operations are prompt-based at inference time.

key_results.optimal_retrieved_memories: ~10-12; performance plateaus then degrades beyond this
key_results.adjustment_advantage_over_second_best: +0.7 reward points, -14 steps at final task group

contributions: Systematic ablation of Build, Retrieve, and Update strategies for agent procedural memory
Proceduralization (combined trajectory + script) as best build strategy
AveFact keyword-averaged retrieval as best retrieval strategy
Adjustment (error-correction reflection) as best update strategy enabling near-linear lifelong learning
Empirical demonstration of cross-model procedural memory transfer (strong→weak) without retraining
limitations_acknowledged: Retrieval restricted to vector-similarity search; BM25 and other methods not explored
Depends on explicit benchmark reward signals; cannot function in real-world settings without ground-truth rewards
limitations_observed: Cross-model transfer only tested in one direction (GPT-4o → smaller model); no bidirectional or same-family tests
No analysis of memory quality/noise as store scales
No cross-domain procedural transfer (e.g., ALFWorld memory on TravelPlanner)
Mechanism for why excess retrieved memories hurt performance is underexplored
No RAG-over-raw-trajectories baseline for fair comparison
relevance_to_thesis: Directly relevant to all three thesis focus areas. For Memory Controller: provides a concrete Build/Retrieve/Update lifecycle for procedural memory with dual-level representation (episodic trace + abstract script). For Educability: Adjustment update strategy operationalizes learning from failure (online self-education), with measurable near-linear improvement curves. For Knowledge Transfer: the GPT-4o → Qwen2.5-14B experiment is direct empirical proof that procedural memory is a transferable distillation artifact independent of model weights — a strong baseline for thesis transfer protocols.
gaps_and_questions: Can procedural memory transfer cross-domain (not just cross-model)?
How to handle memory consolidation and compression as store grows?
Can a weaker model's memories augment a stronger one (reverse transfer)?
Would ontology-structured procedural memory improve retrieval precision over flat key-value?
What is the mechanism behind performance degradation from excess retrieved memories?
poc_ideas: Implement MemP Build+Retrieve+Update pipeline as procedural memory module in thesis memory controller
Test cross-model procedural memory transfer with different model pairs (e.g., Claude→GPT, open→closed)
Compare flat key-value procedural store vs ontology-structured schema for retrieval quality
Extend Adjustment update to include forgetting/deprecation under domain shift
Implement AveFact retrieval with hybrid BM25+dense to improve precision
